cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Poor vehicle understanding, inattention and poor decisions?
cards.back: Poor vehicle understanding, inattention and poor decisions can contribute to crashes.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Manage six surrounding space areas and keep a cushion?
cards.back: Manage six surrounding space areas and keep a cushion on every side of the vehicle.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: On dry pavement, a four-second following gap provides room to?
cards.back: On dry pavement, a four-second following gap provides room to steer or brake around a highway hazard.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Following too closely can leave no way to avoid a crash?
cards.back: Following too closely can leave no way to avoid a crash if the leading vehicle suddenly slows or stops.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: A safe following gap allows a response without a panic?
cards.back: A safe following gap allows a response without a panic stop that could trigger a rear-end collision.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Measure the gap by timing from the leading vehicle's rear bumper passing a fixed point?
cards.back: Measure the gap by timing from the leading vehicle's rear bumper passing a fixed point until your vehicle reaches it; less than four seconds is too close.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Increase the following gap on wet, slippery or?
cards.back: Increase the following gap on wet, slippery or unpaved roads because stopping takes longer.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Leave a larger forward gap when a driver behind wants to?
cards.back: Leave a larger forward gap when a driver behind wants to pass, so that driver has room to return ahead.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Increase the gap behind a driver whose rearward view is blocked,?
cards.back: Increase the gap behind a driver whose rearward view is blocked, because that driver may slow without seeing you.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Leave extra room behind a large vehicle that blocks?
cards.back: Leave extra room behind a large vehicle that blocks the view of the road ahead.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Increase the gap behind a heavily loaded vehicle?
cards.back: Increase the gap behind a heavily loaded vehicle or one towing a trailer.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Allow extra following room when approaching?
cards.back: Allow extra following room when approaching slow vehicles, including bicycles.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Leave additional room behind school buses, taxis, other buses and hazardous-material?
cards.back: Leave additional room behind school buses, taxis, other buses and hazardous-material trucks because they stop at rail crossings or unexpectedly.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Increase following space downhill, where slowing is?
cards.back: Increase following space downhill, where slowing is harder, especially at high speed.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: When stopped uphill, leave room for the vehicle ahead?
cards.back: When stopped uphill, leave room for the vehicle ahead to roll backward as traffic starts.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Side space provides an escape route if another?
cards.back: Side space provides an escape route if another vehicle abruptly enters your lane.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Avoid traveling alongside other vehicles on multilane roads, where views and?
cards.back: Avoid traveling alongside other vehicles on multilane roads, where views and escape routes are blocked and blind spots are likely.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Keep as much separation as?
cards.back: Keep as much separation as possible from oncoming vehicles.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Make room for highway entrants by signaling and moving?
cards.back: Make room for highway entrants by signaling and moving to an inside lane only if safe.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Leave space beside parked vehicles for opening doors,?
cards.back: Leave space beside parked vehicles for opening doors, emerging people or vehicles pulling out.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: If neither side offers an escape path at least eight?
cards.back: If neither side offers an escape path at least eight feet wide, increase the forward following gap.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Normally drive near lane center; with parked cars on the right and oncoming?
cards.back: Normally drive near lane center; with parked cars on the right and oncoming traffic on the left, slow and choose a middle course.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Help preserve rear space by holding a steady speed?
cards.back: Help preserve rear space by holding a steady speed and signaling before slowing for a turn.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: If someone tailgates, move into the?
cards.back: If someone tailgates, move into the right lane when possible.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: With no right lane, wait for a clear road ahead, then gently tap the?
cards.back: With no right lane, wait for a clear road ahead, then gently tap the brakes to reduce speed gradually and encourage a tailgater to pass.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Look for a side escape route?
cards.back: Look for a side escape route before slowing or stopping.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Monitor rear-quarter traffic speed and distance, and turn your head?
cards.back: Monitor rear-quarter traffic speed and distance, and turn your head to check those blind spots before changing lanes.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: A blind spot is an area the driver?
cards.back: A blind spot is an area the driver cannot see without moving the head.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Avoid lingering beside and slightly behind another vehicle; accelerate or?
cards.back: Avoid lingering beside and slightly behind another vehicle; accelerate or fall back to leave its blind spot.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: When passing, clear the other driver's blind spot?
cards.back: When passing, clear the other driver's blind spot as quickly as safety permits.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Look for problems twelve to fifteen seconds ahead, about a city?
cards.back: Look for problems twelve to fifteen seconds ahead, about a city block or a quarter mile at highway speed.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Scan the whole road and its sides instead?
cards.back: Scan the whole road and its sides instead of staring only at the center.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Scan ahead for slower entrants, stopped turning vehicles,?
cards.back: Scan ahead for slower entrants, stopped turning vehicles, hazard warnings and destination signs.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Check the sides wherever traffic streams meet, including?
cards.back: Check the sides wherever traffic streams meet, including intersections, driveways and highway access points.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: At an intersection, look left, right and left again before pulling out because left-side?
cards.back: At an intersection, look left, right and left again before pulling out because left-side traffic is closer and a later check may reveal missed traffic.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: After entering an intersection, check both sides again rather?
cards.back: After entering an intersection, check both sides again rather than assuming other traffic will stop.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: If buildings, shrubs or parked vehicles block the cross-street view,?
cards.back: If buildings, shrubs or parked vehicles block the cross-street view, edge forward slowly until the view clears.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Check rear traffic frequently, especially before?
cards.back: Check rear traffic frequently, especially before changing lanes or reversing.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Entering a highway from a ramp or joining the road from?
cards.back: Entering a highway from a ramp or joining the road from a curb or shoulder counts as a lane change.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Before a lane change, signal, check rear and side mirrors and?
cards.back: Before a lane change, signal, check rear and side mirrors and make sure no vehicle is about to pass.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Use quick shoulder checks as well as mirrors or sensors?
cards.back: Use quick shoulder checks as well as mirrors or sensors to check blind spots before moving lanes.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: A blind-spot check should not take the eyes off the?
cards.back: A blind-spot check should not take the eyes off the road ahead for more than one second.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: On roads with three or more lanes, check every lane before?
cards.back: On roads with three or more lanes, check every lane before changing because another driver may target the same gap.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Before getting into the vehicle to reverse, inspect behind?
cards.back: Before getting into the vehicle to reverse, inspect behind it for children or small objects.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Before backing, turn to look through the rear window rather?
cards.back: Before backing, turn to look through the rear window rather than depending only on mirrors or sensors.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Choose speed using the posted limit, road condition, visibility and?
cards.back: Choose speed using the posted limit, road condition, visibility and traffic flow because no speed is always safe.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Communicate planned speed changes?
cards.back: Communicate planned speed changes to other drivers.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: A posted maximum assumes ideal road,?
cards.back: A posted maximum assumes ideal road, traffic and weather conditions.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Pennsylvania's maximum posted speed limit is?
cards.back: Pennsylvania's maximum posted speed limit is seventy miles per hour

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Interstate maximum-speed signs are posted?
cards.back: Interstate maximum-speed signs are posted after each interchange.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: On other highways, maximum-speed signs appear?
cards.back: On other highways, maximum-speed signs appear at approximately half-mile intervals.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: School-zone speed is limited to fifteen miles per hour while?
cards.back: School-zone speed is limited to fifteen miles per hour while warning lights flash or during the signed times.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Drive below the posted limit in wet, slippery, poorly visible or otherwise less-than-ideal?
cards.back: Drive below the posted limit in wet, slippery, poorly visible or otherwise less-than-ideal conditions; a ticket is possible even below the limit.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: For economical driving, avoid rapid?
cards.back: For economical driving, avoid rapid starts and hard braking.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Avoiding the hottest part of the day can improve mileage because?
cards.back: Avoiding the hottest part of the day can improve mileage because cooler, denser air can help power and efficiency.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: If the onboard-diagnostics lamp comes on, ask the dealer because fuel?
cards.back: If the onboard-diagnostics lamp comes on, ask the dealer because fuel economy may be falling and emissions may be rising.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Use an available ECO setting to smooth throttle inputs, optimize?
cards.back: Use an available ECO setting to smooth throttle inputs, optimize shifting and reduce air-conditioning load on the engine.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Avoid unnecessary idling; when idling is needed, the handbook advises?
cards.back: Avoid unnecessary idling; when idling is needed, the handbook advises neutral or park to reduce engine load.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Reduce driving through transit, cycling, walking, carpooling or combined?
cards.back: Reduce driving through transit, cycling, walking, carpooling or combined errands to save travel costs and fuel.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Night driving reduces vision and can expose the driver to headlight?
cards.back: Night driving reduces vision and can expose the driver to headlight glare and more tired or impaired road users.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Low light reduces distance judgment, color recognition and side vision,?
cards.back: Low light reduces distance judgment, color recognition and side vision, making unexpected road users harder to notice.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Headlights help the driver see and help?
cards.back: Headlights help the driver see and help others see the vehicle.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Clean headlights at?
cards.back: Clean headlights at least weekly.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Use headlights when poor light or blending into gray?
cards.back: Use headlights when poor light or blending into gray surroundings makes the vehicle hard to see.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Use headlights in rain, snow, sleet, hail, fog, smoke or?
cards.back: Use headlights in rain, snow, sleet, hail, fog, smoke or smog, and use low beams in bad weather.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Headlights are required when pedestrians or vehicles cannot?
cards.back: Headlights are required when pedestrians or vehicles cannot be seen one thousand feet ahead.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Headlights must be on between?
cards.back: Headlights must be on between sunset and sunrise.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Use headlights in?
cards.back: Use headlights in work zones.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Weather-related continuous or intermittent windshield-wiper?
cards.back: Weather-related continuous or intermittent windshield-wiper use requires headlights.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Daytime running lamps are insufficient when headlights are required,?
cards.back: Daytime running lamps are insufficient when headlights are required, and the taillights must also be illuminated.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: The handbook lists headlight-use fines starting at twenty-five dollars and?
cards.back: The handbook lists headlight-use fines starting at twenty-five dollars and approaching one hundred dollars with associated costs.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: At night, dim to low beams on noticing oncoming traffic; the law requires low beams within five?
cards.back: At night, dim to low beams on noticing oncoming traffic; the law requires low beams within five hundred feet of an oncoming vehicle or three hundred feet behind another vehicle.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: If oncoming high beams persist after a few brief flashes, look?
cards.back: If oncoming high beams persist after a few brief flashes, look toward the road's right side until the vehicle passes.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Do not keep high beams on to?
cards.back: Do not keep high beams on to retaliate against another driver.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Switch the inside mirror to its night setting?
cards.back: Switch the inside mirror to its night setting if following headlights create uncomfortable glare.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Do not drive faster than a speed that allows stopping?
cards.back: Do not drive faster than a speed that allows stopping within the road illuminated by the headlights.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Low beams illuminate about two?
cards.back: Low beams illuminate about two hundred fifty feet ahead.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: At fifty-five miles per hour, stopping requires more than two?
cards.back: At fifty-five miles per hour, stopping requires more than two hundred fifty feet even on dry pavement.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: To avoid outrunning headlight visibility on a dark road at night, the?
cards.back: To avoid outrunning headlight visibility on a dark road at night, the handbook advises no more than forty-five miles per hour

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Reduce speed on poor road surfaces and take?
cards.back: Reduce speed on poor road surfaces and take slippery turns or curves more slowly.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Pavement may be especially slippery during the first?
cards.back: Pavement may be especially slippery during the first ten to fifteen minutes of rain.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Rain can bring asphalt oil to the surface, and?
cards.back: Rain can bring asphalt oil to the surface, and hot weather makes that slippery-road problem worse.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: In cold wet weather, shaded roads can?
cards.back: In cold wet weather, shaded roads can freeze sooner and dry later.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Hydroplaning occurs when tires lose road grip and?
cards.back: Hydroplaning occurs when tires lose road grip and ride on a film of water.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Hydroplaning can occur at only thirty-five miles per hour in?
cards.back: Hydroplaning can occur at only thirty-five miles per hour in water one tenth of an inch deep.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Worn tires worsen hydroplaning risk, while?
cards.back: Worn tires worsen hydroplaning risk, while slower driving reduces it.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: When hydroplaning, keep both hands on the wheel and slowly release?
cards.back: When hydroplaning, keep both hands on the wheel and slowly release the accelerator; avoid hard braking or sudden turns.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: While hydroplaning, steer slowly only as needed to remain on the?
cards.back: While hydroplaning, steer slowly only as needed to remain on the road and brake gently if braking is necessary.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Snow and ice reduce traction and seriously?
cards.back: Snow and ice reduce traction and seriously affect steering and braking.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Near thirty-two degrees Fahrenheit, rain or sleet can put water over?
cards.back: Near thirty-two degrees Fahrenheit, rain or sleet can put water over ice, creating a surface more slippery than ice alone.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: A wet-looking road with no tire spray from?
cards.back: A wet-looking road with no tire spray from other vehicles may indicate black ice.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: PennDOT urges clearing all snow and ice?
cards.back: PennDOT urges clearing all snow and ice off the vehicle before travel.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: On packed snow, reduce?
cards.back: On packed snow, reduce speed by half.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: On ice, reduce speed?
cards.back: On ice, reduce speed to a crawl.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: On snow- or ice-covered roads, leave about ten?
cards.back: On snow- or ice-covered roads, leave about ten times the normal following space.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Do not use cruise control on slippery roads?
cards.back: Do not use cruise control on slippery roads because continued power can maintain wheelspin.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Adjust speed to avoid meeting other vehicles at?
cards.back: Adjust speed to avoid meeting other vehicles at slippery shaded sections or frosty bridges.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: On icy or packed-snow roads, coast toward an intersection to reach it?
cards.back: On icy or packed-snow roads, coast toward an intersection to reach it after green appears and the vehicles ahead begin moving.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: On a wintry uphill, leave enough distance to avoid?
cards.back: On a wintry uphill, leave enough distance to avoid slowing or stopping behind the leading vehicle.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Select a lower gear before descending a?
cards.back: Select a lower gear before descending a wintry hill for better control.

decks.module: Fog snow squalls and traffic changes

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Do not begin a trip when fog is?
cards.back: Do not begin a trip when fog is so dense that you cannot see.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: If dense fog catches you, pull completely off the road, preferably into?
cards.back: If dense fog catches you, pull completely off the road, preferably into a parking lot, and wait for it to clear.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: While parked waiting out fog, keep the seat?
cards.back: While parked waiting out fog, keep the seat belt fastened and hazard lamps on.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: In fog, slow enough to stop within visible distance and?
cards.back: In fog, slow enough to stop within visible distance and check the speedometer to avoid unrecognized acceleration.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: In fog during day or night, use low beams and available fog lamps rather?
cards.back: In fog during day or night, use low beams and available fog lamps rather than high beams, which reflect glare back toward the driver.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Before snowy travel, clear the windows, hood, trunk and roof so snow does?
cards.back: Before snowy travel, clear the windows, hood, trunk and roof so snow does not block your view or the following driver's windshield.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Clear snow, ice and dirt from headlights,?
cards.back: Clear snow, ice and dirt from headlights, taillights and direction indicators.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Before snowy driving, let the engine warm so the defroster?
cards.back: Before snowy driving, let the engine warm so the defroster can warm the windshield and melt remaining ice.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: In snow, use the wipers and keep the washer reservoir?
cards.back: In snow, use the wipers and keep the washer reservoir full of fluid that will not freeze.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Keep the defroster on for steamed windows and follow?
cards.back: Keep the defroster on for steamed windows and follow the owner's manual for the vehicle's settings.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Use low beams in snowy conditions even in?
cards.back: Use low beams in snowy conditions even in daylight to make the vehicle visible.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: A snow squall can turn clear, dry conditions into near-zero?
cards.back: A snow squall can turn clear, dry conditions into near-zero visibility and a slick road within seconds.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Monitor weather forecasts and transportation message?
cards.back: Monitor weather forecasts and transportation message signs for snow-squall hazards.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Change travel time, route or both to avoid?
cards.back: Change travel time, route or both to avoid snow squalls, particularly high-speed interstate exposure.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: If a squall is approaching or known to be nearby, leave?
cards.back: If a squall is approaching or known to be nearby, leave the roadway and wait for it to pass.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: If caught in a snow squall, slow gradually, activate?
cards.back: If caught in a snow squall, slow gradually, activate hazard lights and avoid slamming the brakes.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: After a collision in a snow squall, remain?
cards.back: After a collision in a snow squall, remain in the vehicle whenever possible.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: A snow-squall warning for the travel route calls?
cards.back: A snow-squall warning for the travel route calls for delaying or altering travel plans.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: When weather requires continuous or intermittent wipers, use headlights and?
cards.back: When weather requires continuous or intermittent wipers, use headlights and illuminated taillights rather than daytime running lamps alone.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: The handbook lists a possible twenty-five-dollar wiper-and-headlight violation fine, with?
cards.back: The handbook lists a possible twenty-five-dollar wiper-and-headlight violation fine, with fees bringing the total toward one hundred dollars.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Match traffic flow while staying?
cards.back: Match traffic flow while staying within the posted limit.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: With a cyclist on the right and oncoming traffic, slow to let the?
cards.back: With a cyclist on the right and oncoming traffic, slow to let the oncoming vehicle pass before moving left to pass the cyclist.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: At an emergency scene, police stop or vehicle-recovery tow truck, move to a nonadjacent lane; if?
cards.back: At an emergency scene, police stop or vehicle-recovery tow truck, move to a nonadjacent lane; if unable, slow at least twenty miles per hour below the posted limit.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Large trucks, farm equipment and horse-drawn vehicles may?
cards.back: Large trucks, farm equipment and horse-drawn vehicles may accelerate slowly when joining traffic.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: On long or steep climbs, trucks typically use flashers?
cards.back: On long or steep climbs, trucks typically use flashers to warn they are moving slowly.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: An orange rear triangle identifies farm or horse-drawn vehicles designed for?
cards.back: An orange rear triangle identifies farm or horse-drawn vehicles designed for speeds of twenty-five miles per hour or less.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Stay well behind tractors and horse-drawn vehicles and do?
cards.back: Stay well behind tractors and horse-drawn vehicles and do not sound the horn to pass.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Brake lights signal slowing or stopping; if other drivers may not expect?
cards.back: Brake lights signal slowing or stopping; if other drivers may not expect braking, quickly tap the pedal three or four times.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: When required to travel below forty miles per hour on a?
cards.back: When required to travel below forty miles per hour on a limited-access highway, use hazard flashers to warn following drivers.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: A turn signal communicates the intended turn but does not?
cards.back: A turn signal communicates the intended turn but does not give the driver priority to make it.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: When driving below thirty-five miles per hour, signal at?
cards.back: When driving below thirty-five miles per hour, signal at least one hundred feet before turning.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: When driving at thirty-five miles per hour or faster, signal?
cards.back: When driving at thirty-five miles per hour or faster, signal at least three hundred feet before turning.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Use hand signals if the?
cards.back: Use hand signals if the vehicle's turn indicators fail.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: A left-turn hand signal extends the left arm?
cards.back: A left-turn hand signal extends the left arm horizontally out from the vehicle.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: A right-turn hand signal bends the left?
cards.back: A right-turn hand signal bends the left arm upward at the elbow.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: The hand signal for slowing or stopping?
cards.back: The hand signal for slowing or stopping directs the left arm downward.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: For a highway breakdown, signal and pull off carefully, park well clear where?
cards.back: For a highway breakdown, signal and pull off carefully, park well clear where others can see, switch on hazards and raise the hood.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: Use the horn when a pedestrian or driver may not see?
cards.back: Use the horn when a pedestrian or driver may not see you or a vehicle appears about to strike you.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: If vehicle control is lost, sound the?
cards.back: If vehicle control is lost, sound the horn to warn other drivers.

cards.front: Which words finish this handbook guidance: When passing a cyclist after oncoming traffic has cleared, leave?
cards.back: When passing a cyclist after oncoming traffic has cleared, leave at least four feet of passing space.
